entries.requires: A person conducting a business or undertaking must ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health and safety of workers and of others put at risk by the work, including safe plant, structures, systems of work and substances.
entries.for_derogations: A derogation does not reduce this standing duty: the company must still show the resulting design is safe so far as is reasonably practicable.

entries.requires: Risks are eliminated so far as reasonably practicable and, failing that, minimised. 'Reasonably practicable' weighs likelihood, degree of harm, knowledge of the risk and of controls, availability and suitability of controls, and cost (cost only after the other factors). Section 18 was read only in part.
entries.for_derogations: A derogation must be justified against this test; cost or convenience alone does not meet it.

entries.requires: A person with management or control of a workplace must ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that the workplace, its entry and exit and anything arising from it are without risks to health and safety.
entries.for_derogations: The site's duty-holder stays responsible for the design as built, whatever internal approval a derogation received.

entries.requires: A term of an agreement or contract that purports to exclude, limit or modify the operation of the Act or a duty under it, or to transfer such a duty, is void.
entries.for_derogations: A statutory duty can be waived neither by contract nor by internal policy; a derogation changes company standards only.

entries.requires: The operator must implement control measures that eliminate the risk of a major incident so far as reasonably practicable, otherwise minimise it, and must minimise the magnitude and consequences of a major incident on site and off site.
entries.for_derogations: A derogation that weakens a major-incident control must still meet the eliminate-or-minimise and off-site consequence tests.

entries.provision: reg 558 (determined MHF); reg 568 heading only (licensed MHF)
entries.requires: The operator of a determined MHF must establish and implement a safety management system so far as reasonably practicable.
entries.for_derogations: The safety management system is the regulated vehicle for demonstrating safety; a derogation process must operate inside it.

entries.requires: A modification of an MHF is any change or proposed change that creates a new unidentified major incident hazard or significantly increases the likelihood or the magnitude of a major incident; examples include changes to plant, structure, process, chemical or inventory.
entries.for_derogations: A design derogation that alters plant, process or inventory can itself be a regulated 'modification'; internal sign-off does not take it outside the definition.

entries.provision: reg 559(1)-(2) (determined MHF); reg 569 (licensed MHF, adds a five-yearly review)
entries.requires: The operator must review and as necessary revise the safety assessment, emergency plan and safety management system when a modification is proposed, when a control measure does not minimise risk so far as reasonably practicable, when a new major hazard risk is identified, and in other listed cases.
entries.for_derogations: The review is triggered when the modification is proposed, before the derogation is implemented.

entries.requires: After a risk-management review the operator must review and as necessary revise the safety case.
entries.for_derogations: A derogation that changes the risk basis must flow through to the safety case, the regulated document.

entries.requires: The operator of a licensed MHF must give the regulator written notice of any change to a material particular of information given for the licence within 14 days of becoming aware of it (example: a change in hazardous chemical quantity).
entries.for_derogations: If a derogation changes information the licence relied on, the regulator must be told within 14 days.

entries.requires: The regulator may exempt the operator of an MHF or proposed MHF from any provision of the Regulations relating to the facility, on the operator's written application.
entries.for_derogations: Only the regulator can set a Regulations duty aside; an internal derogation has no such effect.

entries.requires: The regulator must not grant a reg 688 exemption unless satisfied that Schedule 15 chemicals exceed the threshold only periodically because they are solely in intermediate temporary storage, in containers of no more than 500 kg each, and that health and safety will be at least equivalent to compliance.
entries.for_derogations: A narrow route that requires equivalence; a derogation that lowers safety could not qualify.

entries.requires: The regulator may impose conditions on an exemption (monitoring, records, a stated system of work, reporting) and must issue a document stating the provisions covered, conditions, effect date and duration.
entries.for_derogations: A valid exemption is written, conditioned and time-limited; an internal approval is none of those.

entries.instrument: Workplace Safety and Health (Major Hazard Installations) Regulations 2017 (S 202/2017)
entries.requires: The occupier of a major hazard installation must take all measures necessary to reduce major-accident risk as low as reasonably practicable and limit consequences, and must keep, maintain and implement a safety case. (Read in a third-party mirror of the original 2017 gazette text; the official site refused access. Later amendments not reflected.)
entries.for_derogations: A derogation cannot lower this duty, and the safety case must still demonstrate adequacy with the derogation in place.

entries.instrument: Workplace Safety and Health (Major Hazard Installations) Regulations 2017 (S 202/2017)
entries.requires: The occupier of a registered installation must notify the Commissioner before a modification that may significantly affect major-accident prevention or consequence limitation (a part, a process involving dangerous substances, or the form or quantity of a dangerous substance). (Read in a third-party mirror of the original 2017 gazette text; the official site refused access. Later amendments not reflected.)
entries.for_derogations: A derogation amounting to a significant modification is a notifiable change; internal approval does not replace the prior notice.

entries.instrument: Workplace Safety and Health (Major Hazard Installations) Regulations 2017 (S 202/2017)
entries.requires: The notification must be in the form the Commissioner requires. After such a modification the occupier must not use or operate the modified part, process or substance unless it has reviewed and, if necessary, revised the safety case. (Read in a third-party mirror of the original 2017 gazette text; the official site refused access. Later amendments not reflected.)
entries.for_derogations: The modified item cannot operate until the safety case is reviewed; a derogation cannot waive that gate.

entries.instrument: Workplace Safety and Health (Major Hazard Installations) Regulations 2017 (S 202/2017)
entries.requires: The safety case is reviewed, and revised if necessary, at least every five years, on the Commissioner's direction, and on new safety knowledge (including incident and near-miss analysis), a major-hazard discovery or a significant change to the safety management system; the occupier then reports the outcome to the Commissioner. (Read in a third-party mirror of the original 2017 gazette text; the official site refused access. Later amendments not reflected.)
entries.for_derogations: A derogation that significantly changes the safety management system, or follows new hazard knowledge, triggers a safety case review and a report.

entries.instrument: Workplace Safety and Health (Major Hazard Installations) Regulations 2017 (S 202/2017)
entries.requires: Where an installation in a designated group makes a significant change or a reg 18(2) modification, it reviews its group information and sends revised information to the other occupiers in the group within 14 days. (Read in a third-party mirror of the original 2017 gazette text; the official site refused access. Later amendments not reflected.)
entries.for_derogations: A significant derogation may carry information-sharing duties to neighbouring installations.

entries.instrument: Workplace Safety and Health (Major Hazard Installations) Regulations 2017 (S 202/2017)
entries.requires: Contravening those regulations is an offence (fine up to S$20,000, imprisonment up to two years, or both). The regulations contain no exemption power; reg 16 only allows fee waivers. The Workplace Safety and Health Act exemption section was not read. (Read in a third-party mirror of the original 2017 gazette text; the official site refused access. Later amendments not reflected.)
entries.for_derogations: Acting on an internal derogation is no defence: the duties sit on the occupier.

entries.requires: For a facility holding a listed substance above the Schedule 1 thresholds, the responsible person must prepare an environmental emergency plan covering the s. 4(2) contents, adequate for prevention, preparedness, response and recovery.
entries.for_derogations: A statutory duty triggered by quantity; an internal derogation cannot remove the plan or lower its adequacy standard.

entries.requires: The plan is reviewed at least annually and updated if necessary; simulation exercises are recorded with any plan modifications they lead to. The regulations contain no management-of-change procedure for design modifications.
entries.for_derogations: A derogation that changes facility hazards must be reflected in the plan at the next review at the latest.

entries.requires: An updated notice goes to the Minister within 60 days if the reported facility information changes, or if the maximum expected quantity or container capacity increases by 10% or more.
entries.for_derogations: A derogation that raises inventory or capacity by 10% or more triggers a notice the company cannot waive.

entries.requires: Notices are required when quantity or capacity falls below the thresholds for a year, at least 30 days before ceasing operations for a year or more, and on a transfer of ownership.
entries.for_derogations: Reporting follows physical facts, not internal approvals.

entries.requires: Every submission carries a signed, dated certification of accuracy and completeness and is made electronically.
entries.for_derogations: A derogation-driven notice must be certified accurate, so the internal record must support it.

entries.requires: The only relief is the fixed list of excluded substances in s. 2(2); there is no discretionary exemption, waiver or equivalence mechanism. Annual simulation exercises and five-yearly full-scale exercises are mandatory. No provincial provision was verified.
entries.for_derogations: A company cannot self-grant relief; duties are set aside only if the substance is excluded.

entries.instrument: Occupational Safety and Health Act (Act No. 19611, 8 Aug 2023; KLRI English translation)
entries.requires: Business owners must maintain and promote employee safety and health, including complying with the accident-prevention standards in the Act and its orders.
entries.for_derogations: Statutory standards bind the owner, so an internal derogation cannot fall below them.

entries.instrument: Occupational Safety and Health Act (Act No. 19611, 8 Aug 2023; KLRI English translation)
entries.requires: The owner must identify hazard and risk factors, evaluate whether risk is acceptable and act on the result, and take measures against dangers from machinery, explosive and flammable substances, and energy.
entries.for_derogations: A derogation that leaves unacceptable risk would breach the owner's own risk-assessment and measures duties.

entries.instrument: Occupational Safety and Health Act (Act No. 19611, 8 Aug 2023; KLRI English translation)
entries.requires: An owner with hazardous facilities designated by Presidential Decree must prepare a process-safety report and submit it to the Minister of Employment and Labor for review, and must not operate the facility until notified it is appropriate.
entries.for_derogations: Operating without a reviewed report is prohibited, so a derogation cannot allow operation outside it.

entries.instrument: Occupational Safety and Health Act (Act No. 19611, 8 Aug 2023; KLRI English translation)
entries.requires: The owner and employees must comply with the reviewed process-safety report, and the owner must supplement it without delay whenever a reason arises to amend its content. This is the closest equivalent to management of change in the Act.
entries.for_derogations: A derogation that departs from the reviewed report is a trigger to supplement it; there is no company-level waiver.

entries.instrument: Occupational Safety and Health Act (Act No. 19611, 8 Aug 2023; KLRI English translation)
entries.requires: The Minister reviews the report, notifies the result and may order amendments; the owner keeps it on site and is subject to verification of implementation, and resubmission can be ordered.
entries.for_derogations: The authority, not the company, decides whether a report change is acceptable.

entries.instrument: Occupational Safety and Health Act (Act No. 19611, 8 Aug 2023; KLRI English translation)
entries.provision: Art. 44(1) (scope set by Presidential Decree); Art. 42(3)
entries.requires: The Act contains no discretionary exemption from Arts. 44-46; covered facilities are set by decree. The Enforcement Decree was not read. The KLRI translation is for reference and not legally effective.
entries.for_derogations: Scope is fixed by decree, so a company derogation cannot exempt a covered facility.

entries.requires: Every occupier must ensure, so far as reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare of workers, including safe plant and systems of work, safe handling and storage of substances, and a written safety policy. (Read in a state-government-hosted copy of the Act with the 1987 amendments; later amendments not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: An internal derogation cannot lower this duty; it can only be a documented way of meeting it.

entries.requires: Anyone who designs, manufactures, imports or supplies an article for factory use must ensure, so far as reasonably practicable, that it is safe when properly used, test it and give adequate information; imported articles must meet the Indian or the higher foreign standard. (Read in a state-government-hosted copy of the Act with the 1987 amendments; later amendments not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: A designer or supplier cannot derogate away this statutory design-safety duty.

entries.requires: The State Government may appoint a Site Appraisal Committee to advise on the initial location of a hazardous-process factory or the expansion of one; it recommends within 90 days. (Read in a state-government-hosted copy of the Act with the 1987 amendments; later amendments not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: A derogation that amounts to an expansion of a hazardous-process factory needs State permission, not only internal sign-off.

entries.requires: The occupier of a hazardous-process factory must disclose hazard information to workers, the Chief Inspector, the local authority and the public nearby, inform the Chief Inspector of any change to the safety policy, get approval of the on-site emergency plan, and inform the Chief Inspector of the nature and details of a hazardous process at least thirty days before starting it (failure makes the licence liable to cancellation, s. 41B(6)). (Read in a state-government-hosted copy of the Act with the 1987 amendments; later amendments not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: A derogation that changes the policy, storage or handling measures, or starts a new hazardous process, still triggers notice or approval to the Chief Inspector.

entries.requires: A Safety Committee with equal worker and management representation is mandatory where a hazardous process takes place; only the State Government may exempt an occupier or class of factories, by written order with recorded reasons. (Read in a state-government-hosted copy of the Act with the 1987 amendments; later amendments not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: An exemption that only the State Government can grant; the occupier cannot exempt itself.

entries.requires: Only the State Government may exempt a factory or class of factories from provisions of the Act (except s. 67), and only in a public emergency (a grave threat to the security of India), by Gazette notification, for no more than three months at a time. (Read in a state-government-hosted copy of the Act with the 1987 amendments; later amendments not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: The only general exemption route in the Act; ordinary design or cost reasons cannot ground it and it is not available to the occupier.

entries.requires: Contravening s. 41B, 41C or 41H or the rules under them is punishable with imprisonment up to seven years and a fine up to two lakh rupees, with additional daily fines for a continuing contravention (sub-section (2) raises the term where it continues beyond a year). (Read in a state-government-hosted copy of the Act with the 1987 amendments; later amendments not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: Acting on an internal derogation that breaches those sections exposes the occupier to criminal liability; internal approval is no defence.

entries.instrument: Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (MSIHC)
entries.requires: For an industrial activity meeting the Schedule 1 criteria or isolated storage at or above the Schedule 2 threshold, the occupier must provide evidence that major accident hazards have been identified and adequate steps taken to prevent major accidents and limit their consequences. (Read in a noisy OCR printout of the 1989 text hosted by CPCB/Parivesh; the 1994 and 2000 amendments and the Schedules were not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: A derogation cannot remove the duty to evidence that hazards are identified and controlled; it must itself be evidenced as adequate.

entries.instrument: Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (MSIHC)
entries.requires: An existing industrial activity in which a modification likely to cover major accident hazards has been made is treated as a 'new industrial activity', deemed to commence on the date of the modification. (Read in a noisy OCR printout of the 1989 text hosted by CPCB/Parivesh; the 1994 and 2000 amendments and the Schedules were not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: A derogation that physically changes the plant in a way likely to cover major accident hazards makes the activity 'new' for rules 7-15.

entries.instrument: Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (MSIHC)
entries.requires: The occupier must not undertake a covered activity unless a Schedule 7 report was sent to the concerned authority at least three months beforehand (or a shorter agreed period); an activity that comes to hold a threshold quantity of an additional hazardous chemical is treated as a different activity. (Read in a noisy OCR printout of the 1989 text hosted by CPCB/Parivesh; the 1994 and 2000 amendments and the Schedules were not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: Adding a chemical or quantity through a derogation triggers fresh site notification.

entries.instrument: Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (MSIHC)
entries.requires: If an activity already reported under r. 7(1) changes (threshold quantity up or down, or cessation) in a way that affects the reported particulars, the occupier must forthwith send a further report to the authority. (Read in a noisy OCR printout of the 1989 text hosted by CPCB/Parivesh; the 1994 and 2000 amendments and the Schedules were not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: A change made under a derogation that alters the reported particulars must be reported promptly.

entries.instrument: Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (MSIHC)
entries.requires: The occupier must not undertake a covered activity unless a safety report with the Schedule 8 information has been prepared and sent to the concerned authority at least ninety days before commencing. (Read in a noisy OCR printout of the 1989 text hosted by CPCB/Parivesh; the 1994 and 2000 amendments and the Schedules were not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: The safety report is a pre-condition of operating, and a derogation moves the design away from the filed basis.

entries.instrument: Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (MSIHC)
entries.requires: After making a safety report, the occupier must not modify the activity in a way that could materially affect its particulars unless a further report has been sent to the authority at least ninety days before the modification; a further report is also due within three years of the last. (Read in a noisy OCR printout of the 1989 text hosted by CPCB/Parivesh; the 1994 and 2000 amendments and the Schedules were not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: The central constraint on a derogation under these rules: a change that materially affects the safety-report basis needs an updated report 90 days beforehand.

entries.instrument: Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (MSIHC)
entries.requires: The occupier must prepare and keep up to date an on-site emergency plan that takes account of any modification of the industrial activity, and affected people on site must be informed. (Read in a noisy OCR printout of the 1989 text hosted by CPCB/Parivesh; the 1994 and 2000 amendments and the Schedules were not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: Each derogation that modifies the activity requires the emergency plan to be revised and communicated.

entries.instrument: Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (MSIHC)
entries.requires: Only the Central Government may change the Schedules, by Gazette notification. Rules 1-20 as printed contain no occupier-level exemption or relaxation rule. (Read in a noisy OCR printout of the 1989 text hosted by CPCB/Parivesh; the 1994 and 2000 amendments and the Schedules were not checked.)
entries.for_derogations: The occupier has no self-exemption power; a company derogation cannot waive any duty.
